questions.question: **The latency's real lever is the model, and it needs your call.** Evidence: the prompt is small and constant (~1.7–2.1k input tokens), `toolChoice: { any: {} }` is already forced at `bedrock.provider.ts:197`, so the model is *required* to call a tool — and it still emitted **13,176 output tokens** on one question. Those are preamble/reasoning wrapped around the tool call, which is what `mistral-large-3-675b` (a reasoning model) does. A `maxTokens` cap alone is risky: if the cap hits before the tool block, `toolUse` is undefined and the code returns `noToolUse` — turning slow successes into fast failures. Decision 0027 fixes provider and region only, so the model family is unpinned and nobody has chosen it deliberately.
options: Switch to a fast instruct model, amend 0027 (Recommended)
Keep this model, add a guarded cap + retry
Leave the model alone, ship streaming only
questions.chosen: Keep this model, add a guarded cap + retry

questions.question: **The `Freshness unavailable` pill is a hard-coded stub** — `app-shell.tsx:174` renders static text with `aria-disabled="true"`, computing nothing, like the greyed-out search box beside it. The underlying data does exist: `selectionExecutor.freshness()` queries the warehouse and provenance already carries `dataAsOf`, but no route exposes it to the shell.
options: Wire it to real warehouse freshness (Recommended)
questions.chosen: Wire it to real warehouse freshness (Recommended)
